results.correct_value: Class 3-4 (sustained Class 3 with short Class 4 steps)
results.evidence: A detailed trip-report site titles the North Twin west ridge '4th' class; a scrambling guide page headlines it Class 3 but says sections of the west ridge run Class 3-4 (Class 5 means off route); search summaries of other route pages describe ~1,500 ft of sustained Class 3 and Class 4. The row's own beta, itinerary, climbing_route and waypoint all say Class 3-4, and the sibling West Ridge entry for the same line is graded Class 3-4; only grade and rock_grade said plain Class 3.

dist_km 9.7 (about 6.0 mi) is the approach to the base of the scrambling (logging roads plus clearcut to the ridge, ~5-6 mi as the itinerary itself says), while the waypoints and approach prose give the full car-to-summit distance of ~7-7.3 mi including the ridge; two different quantities, and no source establishes a different one-way approach figure.

results.fact: High camp location, elevation and permit
results.evidence: Two genuine camps exist: the Ruth Arm/glacier-toe camps on Forest Service land (~5,800-5,900 ft, no park permit), which the Campsite waypoint and bivy[0] describe, and the ~6,600 ft camp at the notch northwest of Ruth's summit inside the park (permit required), which the itinerary uses; access.permit explicitly explains both. A Mountaineers route summary confirms the 6,600 ft notch camp, and a guide-service route profile describes a separate lower camp used for two-day ascents. The bivy side of the dispute belongs to the camping clean-up.

The only dissenting claim is inside bivy[3].notes ('most parties go in June or July'); seasonal_guidance, best_season and climate agree on late July-August. bivy[] is owned by the camping clean-up, so no patch is written here.

results.fact: Distance to the Sulphur Creek crossing
results.correct_value: The crossing is at the very start of the trail, well under a mile in (the approach's 0.3-0.4 mile stands); the waypoint's 1 mile is wrong and no source gives an exact figure, so its distance is set to unknown.
results.evidence: A Park Butte trail guide says the hike starts by crossing Sulphur Creek on a wooden bridge right from the trailhead; a trail database page says the path begins along dirt before crossing Sulphur Creek into Schreibers Meadow, and another summary says the meadow is entered about half a mile in, after the crossing. None supports a crossing at 1 mile; none gives an exact decimal, so distMi is nulled rather than replaced by an interpolated value.

results.fact: Character of the final climb to the summit
results.correct_value: The finish to Sherman Peak is a steepening snow slope (loose rock if bare), not an easy ridge walk.
results.evidence: A country-highpoints trip report describes front-pointing up steep, icy slopes to Sherman's summit ridge; a SummitPost trip report of an ascent from the saddle at the base of the west ridge placed a picket 30-40 ft below the summit on the steep final pitch.
